messages:
Marta: FYI — we're seeing a sharp uptick in 5xx from hosted API gateway since ~03:14 UTC. Error mix: 502 gateway errors, 504 timeouts, and 500 with 'downstream timeout'. Started right after the canary roll at 03:12. Customer support pinged: PartnerX reports timeouts and retries flooding them.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started at 03:12 UTC by Devon. service=hosted-api target=v2.46 canary_weight=10%

Devon: I flipped fast_rollout=true as part of the rollout recipe at 03:10. Target was 10% canary. I didn't get any alerts during pipeline.

Marta: Quick data points — error rate on /v1/generate jumped from 0.6% -> 11% over 5m. P95 latency doubled. Trace snippets show upstreams returning 504 after 30s.

Jai (oncall): Can we confirm actual canary weight? There was a previous bug where the binary-flag propagated wrong. Running check now: `rwoodctl rollout status --service hosted-api --name canary`

Samir: Output from rwoodctl: 
```
name: hosted-api-canary
desired_weight: 10
actual_weight: 40
status: updating
```
That's... not expected. Something bumped weight.

Lisa: OMG, that explains the scale. If actual_weight became 40% then 4x the traffic hit the new runtime variant which has a regression in header propagation.

Marta: Any idea why the weight drifted? Devon, did you trigger staged-rollout with a policy override?

Devon: I only triggered `fast_rollout=true` via the feature-flag service. I didn't touch the orchestration API directly. I did see the flag evaluate as true for the canary service in prod. I did not expect it to bump to 40%.

Jai (oncall): Looking at orchestration audit log: `flag_evaluator[:memory]` had a race when simultaneously applying two updates (auto-scaler and rollout controller). The controller wrote new weight after seeing the flag, but the auto-scaler reconciled and applied a consolidated weight. There is a bug where consolidate() multiplies partial weights in rare races.

Samir: Reproducer for the issue (from staging):
```
# simulate concurrent updates
curl -X POST https://orch/rpc/rollout -d '{"name":"hosted-api","weight":10}'
curl -X POST https://orch/rpc/rollout -d '{"name":"hosted-api","scale":4}'
# sometimes ends up with weight 40
```

Marta: Ok next steps — immediate mitigation: pause/rollback canary, remove flag, scale down the canary variant, and coordinate with support for customer comms. Jai, can you take rollback?

Jai (oncall): On it. Running: `rwoodctl rollout pause hosted-api --canary` -> returned success. Now initiating rollback: `rwoodctl rollback hosted-api --to-version v2.45 --force`

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated at 03:28 UTC. Target state: all traffic -> v2.45.

Lisa: I'm updating Support: sending message to PartnerX with ETA for mitigation and asking them to hold off retries. Samir, please check if retries from clients produced billing anomalies.

Samir: Support notes: PartnerX reported ~12 timeout errors and 7 retries within 6 minutes. Billing pipeline flagged an increase in request counts for some customers — likely due to automatic retries. I'll run dedupe job after stabilization.

Devon: Also found a config leak in the feature-flag service: the 'fast_rollout' key was accidentally set in the global namespace instead of the canary namespace. That allowed other controllers to pick it up. I'll open a PR to add namespace scoping and a safety check.

Marta: Good. After rollback completes, we need to: 1) validate traffic is back to v2.45, 2) run a smoke test load (curl + streaming), 3) monitor 5xx for 30m, 4) run billing dedupe.

Jai (oncall): Rollback finished at 03:36 UTC. Verifying service state: `rwoodctl rollout status --service hosted-api` -> `active_version: v2.45, actual_weight: 100`

Marta: Metrics look good — 5xx dropped back to baseline within 4m of rollback. P95 returned to near previous.

Lisa: Support update sent to PartnerX and to the incident channel. They've accepted our explanation and want an RCA.

Devon: Filed PR #789 to add namespace scoping + guard in flag-evaluator. Also added an assertion in the consolidation logic to avoid multiplicative weight merges.

Samir: Billing follow-up — running dedupe for requests between 03:12 and 03:40 for customers flagged by Support. Will follow up in the billing channel.

Marta: I'll open an incident doc and link playbooks + timeline. Tagging the infra and rollout teams for postmortem.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-17489, severity=high, owner=Marta, timeline_link=https://redwood/incidents/INC-2024-17489

Marta: Summary: rapid rollout + feature-flag namespace leak + consolidation race -> actual canary weight spike -> regression in new runtime variant -> surge in 5xx/timeouts. Resolved by rollback and feature-flag fix. Postmortem and action items assigned.

Jai (oncall): Closing loop — monitoring for 1h. If anything reappears ping @oncall. :thumbsup:

Marta: Thanks all for the quick turnaround.
